<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The pursuit of human-level artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly advanced the development of autonomous agents and Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are now widely utilized as decision-making agents for their ability to interpret instructions, manage sequential tasks, and adapt through feedback. This review examines recent developments in employing LLMs as autonomous agents and tool users and comprises seven research questions. We only used the papers published between 2023 and 2025 in conferences of the A* and A-ranked and Q1 journals. A structured analysis of the LLM agents’ architectural design principles, dividing their applications into single-agent and multi-agent systems, and strategies for integrating external tools is presented. In addition, the cognitive mechanisms of LLMs, including reasoning, planning, and memory, and the impact of prompting methods and fine-tuning procedures on agent performance are also investigated. Furthermore, we have evaluated current benchmarks and assessment protocols and provided an analysis of 68 publicly available datasets to assess the performance of LLM-based agents in various tasks. In conducting this review, we have identified critical findings on verifiable reasoning of LLMs, the capacity for self-improvement, and the personalization of LLM-based agents. Finally, we have discussed ten future research directions to overcome these gaps.</jats:p>
title: From language to action: a review of large language models as autonomous agents and tool users

items.abstract: <jats:p>Large Action Models (LAMs) represent a significant evolution from traditional Large Language Models (LLMs) by not only understanding natural language but also autonomously performing tasks in real-world applications. This paper explores the core differences between LLMs and LAMs, emphasizing the expanded capabilities of LAMs to handle complex, multi-step tasks that require interaction with external systems, sensors, and multimodal inputs. LAMs leverage advanced techniques in neuro-symbolic AI, combining neural networks for pattern recognition with symbolic reasoning for logical task execution. The paper highlights key applications of LAMs across industries, including healthcare, manufacturing, customer service, and smart city infrastructure, where their ability to autonomously act, learn from feedback, and interact with both digital and physical environments offers substantial advantages. The role of frameworks like the LAM Simulator is also discussed, illustrating how it accelerates LAM training by automating data generation and providing real-time feedback. This research underscores the transformative potential of LAMs in driving automation and enhancing efficiency across various sectors.</jats:p>
title: From Language to Action : A Study on the Evolution of Large Language Models to Large Action Models

items.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has revolutionized natural language processing, yet these models remain fundamentally constrained by their reliance on static training corpora, resulting in knowledge cutoffs, factual hallucinations, and an inability to access real-time or proprietary information. This paper addresses these critical limitations by proposing a novel architectural framework for integrating LLMs with autonomous search agents to create hybrid systems capable of advanced information retrieval. Moving beyond simplistic retrievalaugmented generation (RAG) approaches, this research introduces a dynamic orchestration layer wherein LLMs function not merely as answer generators but as strategic reasoning cores that decompose complex queries, formulate search intentions, and delegate execution to specialized autonomous agents. These agents, equipped with tool-use capabilities, navigate heterogeneous information landscapes-including public web repositories, deep web databases, and structured knowledge bases-through iterative search, filtering, and evidence accumulation. The framework incorporates a bidirectional feedback loop: search results inform and refine the LLM's reasoning process, while the LLM's evolving understanding guides subsequent search strategies. We evaluate the integrated system against traditional LLM baselines and simple RAG implementations using benchmarks that test multi-step reasoning, temporal awareness, and information synthesis across disparate sources. Results demonstrate significant improvements in factual accuracy (reducing hallucinations by approximately 40%), query completion rates for complex multi-source requests, and the ability to answer time-sensitive questions requiring upto-date information. This work contributes a principled methodology for creating transparent, verifiable, and dynamically knowledgeable AI systems, with implications for academic research, enterprise intelligence, and the democratization of advanced information access. The proposed integration paradigm establishes a foundation for the next generation of intelligent information retrieval systems that combine the reasoning depth of LLMs with the breadth and timeliness of autonomous search.</jats:p>
title: Integrating Large Language Models with Autonomous Search Agents for Advanced Information Retrieval
